output:
**What I found:** The first wave can't start tonight. The preflight record can't pass the checker (the record calls this FAIL). Five things block it: the record names no plan revision, it covers a window six days ago, the repository token expired on 2026-11-14 03:00Z, the clerk account is shared between two packages that run at the same time, and the plan has neither `unattended` nor `needs`.

**Why it matters:** If the run starts as is, it loses repository access as soon as it needs it, and P1 and P2 log in as the same clerk at once. The gate would also refuse the result with `PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED`, so a night of work could never reach the merge boundary. Fixing it means amending the plan, which needs a new plan check and a new preflight record before 22:00.

**Do this first:**
1. Amend `.alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json`: set `execution.unattended: true` and give each package `needs`, including an `environment` need for `npm test`. Then re-run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root . --approved`.
2. Rewrite `.alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json` (details below), then run `check_orchestration.py preflight .alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .`. Start only on `PASS`.

**What I did not check:**
- The preflight checker itself. I have no shell here, so everything below comes from reading the files against `references/autonomy-preflight.md`. Running the preflight command in step 2 closes this.
- The earlier plan-check PASS. There's no saved output, so I couldn't confirm it, and it only applies to the plan as an attended run. The amended plan check in step 1 closes this.
- Whether the host stays awake and the runtime stays open from 22:00 to 08:00. A person has to confirm this.

---

```text
Execution:  multi-agent
Strategy:   dependency-aware
Agents:     3 (P1 agent-a, P2 agent-b, P3 agent-c reviewer); cap 2 concurrent, delegation depth 1
Packages:   wave 1 [P1, P2] (independent, disjoint write sets) → wave 2 [P3] (reviews P1, P2)
Reason:     P1 and P2 have no dependency path and write disjoint sets; P3 is an independent reviewer
Plan check: Not run in this session. User reports PASS, but that applies to the plan before amendment; the unattended amendment needs a new check
Preflight:  Not run (no shell available). Reading the record, it would return FAIL
```

| # | Code | Evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `SCHEMA` / `PREFLIGHT_STALE` | `preflight.json` has no `plan` field (`digest`, `base`), so it isn't tied to any plan revision |
| 2 | `NEEDS_UNDECLARED` | `plan.json` has no `execution.unattended`. None of P1–P3 has `needs`. P1 and P2 have `command` criteria (`npm test -- orders`, `npm test -- shipments`) but no `environment` need |
| 3 | `PREREQUISITE_UNCOVERED` | No preflight entry has `covers` |
| 4 | Window wrong | `window` is 2026-11-13T22:00Z to 2026-11-14T08:00Z. Tonight is 2026-11-19 22:00 to 2026-11-20 08:00 (zone not stated; the record uses `Z`). Every expiry has to be checked again against the real window |
| 5 | `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRES` | A1 `REPO_TOKEN` `expires: 2026-11-14T03:00:00Z`. That is before the recorded window ends, and it has already passed. E1 proved the old token, so a new token needs a new probe |
| 6 | `ACCOUNT_CONFLICT` | U1 (order clerk, can write, not shared) lists `packages: [P1, P2]`, and both run in wave 1. Each package needs its own clerk account with its own reset command and probe |
| 7 | Probe mismatch (judgment) | E4 runs `probe:login -- clerk-b auditor`, but the record has no clerk-b. Check that E4 proves the U3 auditor login and role, not some other account |

Passes on reading (the checker still has to confirm): both increments are ready (I1 `READY`, I2 `PARTLY-READY` with `reversible: true`). D1 and D2 were decided by a human; D2 goes to the merge-boundary confirmation queue. Every probe passed at base `3f9c2e1`. The baseline command V1 `npm test` passed (E6). Bounds and escalation are recorded, and E7 recorded a test delivery. Human steps happen only `before` and at `end`. The record holds secret names, not values.

Things a person has to decide; the checker can't:
- **Bounds.** The record doesn't say whether the lead may raise the retry or rework bounds overnight. Add it as a decision (answered, or `stop`).
- **Order.** I2 is only `PARTLY-READY`, so it's the riskier increment and its failure should show up early. P1 and P2 already run together in wave 1, so no reordering is needed.

```text
Gate:        Not run; first wave not started
Verified:    None
Unverified:  REQ-12-AC1, REQ-13-AC1, P3-AC1 (run not started)
Open:        1–6 above block the start; 7 needs a person to check the probe
Merge:       human approval required
```
